title: A deployment requirement can name the environment variables it needs
description:
SPIDR grandchild B of task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1 (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05). This row exists because the parent's DoD 3 assumed structure that DOES NOT EXIST, and global rail 6 requires the gap be closed by a prerequisite row measured symbol by symbol rather than by narrowing the DoD.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04). The parent says "the compiler emits the deployment requirements' variable names, read from the contract rather than a hand-kept list". There is no such field. A deployment requirement is exactly:
  { dependsOnRequirementIds, priority, requirementId, statement, supersedesRequirementId }
(apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/gate1-v2-test-fixture.ts:7-15, mirrored at apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/compiler.test.ts:45-48). Confirmed absent by `grep -rn "variableName|environmentVariable|requiredVariables|envVar" packages/contracts/src apps/daemon/src/planning` returning ZERO hits. Also note `deploymentRequirements` does not appear in packages/contracts at all - the shape lives in apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/gate1-contract-shape.ts (:14 in the section roster, :172 in the validator) and is mirrored daemon-side.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: adding the variable-names carrier to the deployment requirement shape and its validator, so a requirement can state the environment variable names it needs. Grandchild C consumes it.

SIZE THIS BEFORE YOU WIDEN ANYTHING. `grep -rln "dependsOnRequirementIds" apps packages --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` returns 27 FILES. A REQUIRED field on that shape is a 27-file change, far past the 10-file ceiling. An OPTIONAL field that defaults to empty is the tractable shape and is very likely the right answer - but MEASURE the actual roster your chosen shape forces before writing code, and if it still exceeds the ceiling, SPLIT rather than submitting over it. Do not make the field required to be tidy.

FIELD SEMANTICS. Names only, never values - this data is contract text that gets displayed, stored and published. An empty or absent list means the requirement names no variables, which must remain the overwhelmingly common case and must not make any existing contract invalid.

NOT IN SCOPE: reading the names back, the unset-set report, `.env.example`, delivery, UI. Those are grandchild C and the parent's child 3.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: A deployment requirement can carry the environment variable NAMES it needs, and the shape validator (apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/gate1-contract-shape.ts) accepts it. Assert a requirement WITH names validates and a requirement carrying a VALUE-shaped entry does not - names only.

EVERY EXISTING CONTRACT STAYS VALID. A requirement with no names, and one with the field absent entirely, both validate exactly as today. Assert both explicitly: this is the property that keeps the field optional and the blast radius small, and it is the one a required-field implementation silently breaks.

The forced-edit roster is MEASURED AND STATED before implementation: run `grep -rln "dependsOnRequirementIds" apps packages --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` (27 files at filing) plus a shape grep for the literal requirement object in test expectations, and record which files your chosen field shape actually forces. If that set exceeds the 10-file ceiling, STOP and split - do not submit over it.

The daemon-side mirror of the requirement shape agrees with the control-room one, asserted rather than assumed - the shape is transcribed in both and a divergence is invisible until a contract round-trips.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. The control-room leg is not optional: the shape and its validator live under apps/control-room, which the root vitest lane does not cover.
taskRails: NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES. This is contract text: it is displayed, stored, and reaches a published repository through grandchild C. A value here is a value published.
OPTIONAL, NOT REQUIRED, unless you measure that required fits the ceiling. 27 files reference the requirement shape; a required field is a 27-file change and a split.
MEASURE THE FORCED-EDIT ROSTER BEFORE WRITING CODE and split at plan time if it exceeds the ceiling - a worker discovering it at step 5 is the failure this rail exists to prevent.
DO NOT CONSUME THE FIELD HERE. The unset-set report and .env.example are grandchild C.

implementationPlan.description:
THE CORE VALIDATOR (packages/core/src/product-contract/product-contract-v2-admission.ts).

Add `DEPLOYMENT_REQUIREMENT_KEYS` = the existing five plus the new name, and validate deploymentRequirements by ACCEPTING EITHER SHAPE:
  exact(value, REQUIREMENT_KEYS) || exact(value, DEPLOYMENT_REQUIREMENT_KEYS)
That is the only shape that satisfies DoD 1 and DoD 2 together, because `exact` at planning-snapshot.ts:182 is STRICT: `Reflect.ownKeys(value).length === keys.length`. A key added to a single roster is a key made REQUIRED, and every contract lacking it becomes invalid.

Leave `REQUIREMENT_KEYS` and the five other requirement sections UNTOUCHED — they share the same validator and none of them is this row's subject.

VALIDATE THE NAMES THEMSELVES, since this is the boundary that keeps a value out (rail 1): each entry is a string, matches an environment-variable name grammar (the conventional `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` unless you measure a reason to differ), is bounded in length, and the list is bounded in count and free of duplicates. A permissive validator here is what lets `DB_PASSWORD=hunter2` be stored as a NAME.

Refuse with the existing refusal machinery (`invalid()` / `productContractV2Refusal`) — do not mint a new code path or a new layer constant.
implementationPlan.note:
THE CORE VALIDATOR accepts EITHER SHAPE for deploymentRequirements only. `REQUIREMENT_KEYS` (:50) and the five other requirement sections are byte-for-byte untouched - `git diff` shows the only change at the section-wiring site is the deployment line (:493-495); functional/nonFunctional/ux/security/technology still pass `readRequirement`.

WHAT LANDED in product-contract-v2-admission.ts:
- `DEPLOYMENT_REQUIREMENT_KEYS` (:54-57) = the five plus `environmentVariableNames`, sorted.
- `ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_NAME = /^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$/` (:59) - POSIX portable name grammar.
- `readEnvironmentVariableNames` (:216-228).
- `readDeploymentRequirement` (:231-241).
- deployment section rewired to `readDeploymentRequirement` (:493-495).
- `type ProductContractV2DeploymentRequirement` added to the existing import block, alphabetically placed.

THE EITHER-SHAPE MECHANIC, and why it delegates rather than duplicates: `readDeploymentRequirement` first tests `exact(value, DEPLOYMENT_REQUIREMENT_KEYS)`. If that fails it hands the value straight to the UNMODIFIED `readRequirement`, so a 5-key requirement takes exactly today's code path and today's refusal codes - that is DoD 2 by construction, not by a parallel implementation that could drift. If it succeeds, it destructures the names off and passes the remaining 5-key rest object to the SAME `readRequirement`, so priority/statement/id/cycle rules are enforced by one implementation for both shapes. No new refusal code, no new layer constant, no change to `readRequirement`'s signature (which `readSortedItems` calls with a single argument at :148).

NAME VALIDATION - this is the boundary that keeps a value out (rail 1). Each entry goes through the file's existing `readText` at the new `maxEnvironmentVariableNameBytes` bound, so it inherits the same discipline as every other string in the contract: NUL-free, `isWellFormed()`, NFC-normalized, trimmed, byte-bounded. THEN the grammar `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$` runs on top. Composition means `"DB_PASSWORD=hunter2"`, `"DB_PASSWORD: hunter2"`, `"DB_PASSWORD hunter2"`, a lowercase name, a leading digit, an embedded quote/newline/NUL and an empty string are all refused. The list is bounded in count by `maxEnvironmentVariableNames` (256) and duplicates are impossible because the reader requires STRICTLY INCREASING order (`result.at(-1)! >= name.value` refuses), reusing the exact idiom `readSortedRefs` (:100) already uses - so unsorted and duplicate are one rule, not two.

REASON CODES ARE DETERMINISTIC AND DISTINCT (global rail 1 - step 5 asserts these, not merely "it refused"):
  non-array, bad grammar, unsorted, duplicate, empty string -> PRODUCT_CONTRACT_V2_PROVENANCE_INVALID
  name over 128 bytes, list over 256 entries -> PRODUCT_CONTRACT_V2_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
  (empty string routes to INVALID, not VACUOUS, because `validRef` at planning-snapshot.ts:209 rejects "" before the trim check - traced, not assumed.)

CODEC MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: `canonicalText` (product-contract-v2-codec.ts:64-76) walks `Object.keys(record).sort()` generically, so the new key encodes, decodes and enters the digest with no codec edit. `snapshotDataBounded` depth is 4 for the new array, under `maxSnapshotDepth` 8.

implementationPlan.description:
THE ACCEPTANCE AND REJECTION ARMS (DoD 1 and DoD 2), on BOTH sides. Note the test homes, which are not where you would guess: `product-contract-v2-admission.ts` has NO test file of its own and its v2 arms live in `packages/core/src/product-contract/product-contract-v2-codec.test.ts` — extend that. `gate1-contract-shape.ts` has none either, so create `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/gate1-contract-shape.test.ts`. Put the SAME cases on both sides.

DoD 2 FIRST, because it is the property a required-field implementation silently breaks. Assert BOTH forms explicitly:
(a) a deployment requirement with the names field ABSENT ENTIRELY validates exactly as today;
(b) one with an EMPTY list validates.
And assert that an existing full contract fixture — apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/gate1-v2-test-fixture.ts, mirrored at apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/compiler.test.ts:45-48 — still validates UNCHANGED. Absence and emptiness are different states and only one of them is the common case.

DoD 1: a requirement WITH names validates, and a requirement carrying a VALUE-SHAPED entry does NOT. Make the rejection concrete rather than gestural: `["DB_PASSWORD=hunter2"]`, `["DB_PASSWORD: hunter2"]`, a lowercase name, a name with a space, an empty string, a duplicate, and a list past the bound. Assert each refuses with its specific reason — never merely that validation failed.
